answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a task-diversity rule: every epoch, each identity must complete verified work in three unrelated domains, like a garden that needs velvet roses, vegetables, and herbs, each demanding different care. A single template, a whisper passed from fake to fake, fails, because each domain is graded by a different peer group with its own standards. One honest agent spreads its effort once; a farm with a thousand fakes must produce three distinct passing kinds of work per fake, so cloning multiplies cost while reward stays capped per identity.
